newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar gains as foreigners sell dollars.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar gains as foreigners sell dollars.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed slightly firmer at 474.60/475.10 per dollar Wednesday, compared to 475.25/475.70 per dollar Tuesday, as foreign investors sold foreign currency to buy into central bank papers, dealers said.
"The supply (of foreign currency) was so large that all the banks lowered their rate and the Central Bank did not need to intervene," one trader said.
Another trader said the local branch of Dutch bank ING sold large amounts of foreign currency on the interbank market.
An ING trader confirmed to Reuters that it had sold a lot of dollars "for foreign clients seeking bolivars to buy Monetary Stabilization (TEM) bills."
The Central Bank sold 90 billion bolivars ($189 million) worth of TEM bills at its weekly auction Wednesday.
Other traders noted that dollar supply had also increased due to greater interest in Venezuelan stocks on the Caracas Stock Exchange in recent sessions.
